feature: Home parity — one page, drawn twice
note: One route, photographed at both widths, because the whole claim of this round is that the two widths draw the same page. Desktop and mobile had drifted into two: the resume block and Commitments existed on desktop only, and `Your decks` — a second, worse /decks — carried the phone. The contact sheet is the artefact that shows it, since a review reads a diff and cannot see a block that is absent at one width. The `shares` block names `CommitmentsCard`, whose whole point this round is that the phone mounts the SAME component rather than a phone copy of it — so both rows name Home's own view, which is where it is rendered. The resume block cannot be checked that way: one route draws it, so an import-equality check would assert a sameness the feature does not claim. Its two widths are a geometry question, and `pnpm probe:home` answers it — four rows 2×2 above 1000px and stacked below, the stamp in every row, and Commitments last on the phone.
